templates.pattern: A file of [SIZE] MB needs to be transmitted over a network with a bandwidth of [BW] MB/s. Calculate the transmission delay in seconds.
templates.explanation:
Transmission delay = file size ÷ bandwidth
= [SIZE] ÷ [BW]
= [RESULT] s

Transmission delay is the time taken to push all bits of the file onto the link. A faster bandwidth reduces transmission delay proportionally.

templates.pattern: A file has a size of [SIZE] KB. Calculate the size of the file in bits.
templates.explanation:
File size in bits = KB × 1024 × 8
= [SIZE] × 1024 × 8
= [SIZE] × 8192
= [RESULT] bits

1 KB = 1024 bytes and 1 byte = 8 bits. Always convert to bits before calculating transmission times.

templates.pattern: A file of [SIZE] MB is downloaded at a speed of [SPEED] MB/s. Calculate the download time in seconds.
templates.explanation:
Download time = file size ÷ download speed
= [SIZE] ÷ [SPEED]
= [RESULT] s

Download time depends on both the file size and the available bandwidth. Larger files and slower connections both increase download time.

templates.pattern: A file of [SIZE] KB is divided into packets of [PACKET] KB each. Calculate the number of packets needed to transmit the file.
templates.explanation:
Number of packets = file size ÷ packet size
= [SIZE] ÷ [PACKET]
= [RESULT] packets

Packet switching divides data into smaller units for transmission. Smaller packets reduce the impact of errors but increase header overhead.

templates.pattern: A network has a propagation delay of [PROP] ms and a transmission delay of [TRANS] ms. Calculate the total latency in ms.
templates.explanation:
Total latency = propagation delay + transmission delay
= [PROP] + [TRANS]
= [RESULT] ms

Latency is the total time for data to travel from sender to receiver. Propagation delay depends on distance and transmission delay depends on file size and bandwidth.

templates.pattern: A signal travels [DIST] km through a cable at a speed of [SPEED] × 10⁵ km/s. Calculate the propagation delay in milliseconds.
templates.explanation:
Propagation delay = distance ÷ speed
= [DIST] km ÷ ([SPEED] × 10⁵ km/s)
= [DIST] ÷ ([SPEED] × 10⁵) s
= [RESULT] ms

Propagation delay depends on the physical distance and the speed of the signal in the medium. Light in fibre travels at about 2 × 10⁵ km/s.

templates.pattern: A network connection has a bandwidth of [BW] Mbits/s. Calculate the bandwidth in Mbytes/s.
templates.explanation:
Bandwidth in MB/s = bandwidth in Mb/s ÷ 8
= [BW] ÷ 8
= [RESULT] MB/s

Bandwidth is often quoted in bits per second but file sizes are usually in bytes. Always divide by 8 to convert between bits and bytes.

templates.pattern: A data transmission sends [PKTS] packets each of size [SIZE] KB. Calculate the total data transmitted in KB.
templates.explanation:
Total data = number of packets × packet size
= [PKTS] × [SIZE]
= [RESULT] KB

This is useful for calculating the total bandwidth used by a transmission. In practice each packet also has a header which adds overhead.

templates.pattern: A file of [SIZE] MB is stored on a hard drive. Calculate the storage required in KB.
templates.explanation:
Storage in KB = MB × 1024
= [SIZE] × 1024
= [RESULT] KB

1 MB = 1024 KB. Understanding unit conversions is essential in Computer Science — always be careful whether you are working in bits, bytes, KB, MB or GB.

templates.pattern: A network has a maximum bandwidth of [BW] Mbits/s. A file of [SIZE] MB is transmitted. Calculate the minimum transmission time in seconds.
templates.explanation:
Transmission time = file size in bits ÷ bandwidth
= ([SIZE] × 8) Mbits ÷ [BW] Mbits/s
= [SIZE*8] ÷ [BW]
= [RESULT] s

Note: file size must be converted from MB to Mbits by multiplying by 8 before dividing by bandwidth.
